story.what_it_does: TCS is a large IT services company that builds, runs and modernises technology systems for clients. In FY26 it had revenue of ₹267,021 crore and about 584,500 staff, and by September 2026 about 598,000. It also reports a growing AI services business, at US$3.1 billion annualised in Q2 FY27.
story.plans: Management wants operating margin to exit FY27 above 25% and keeps a long-term aim of 26-28%. It plans to add 50,000 seats in Tier-1 and Tier-2 Indian cities, and to build AI data centres (HyperVault), with revenue starting about 18-24 months after a contract is signed. It does not give revenue or earnings guidance.
story.moat: The notes point to scale and client relationships: a US$40.7 billion order book in FY26, repeated mega deal wins, and stable attrition around 13-14%. The notes also warn that AI-driven price deflation and new deep-tech competitors may pressure traditional services pricing, so the strength of this moat is not proven in the notes.

scenarios.story: Constant-currency growth stays positive for several quarters, large deal wins turn into revenue, and AI revenue keeps climbing. Margin then recovers toward the 25% exit target and beyond.
signals_to_watch: Constant-currency sequential revenue growth above the 0.4-0.5% seen in Q1 and Q2 FY27
Operating margin moving back above 24% toward the 25% exit target

scenarios.story: Growth stays slow, at about 0.5% a quarter in constant currency, with margin around 24% as wage costs and subcontracting weigh. Deal wins stay near US$9-10 billion a quarter while rupee growth is helped by currency.
